title: SmimeError is not Serialize/Deserialize while all other public types are — inconsistent API contract
description:
## Problem

The `smime-tree` CLAUDE.md invariant states: 'Both crates: owned, lifetime-free public types. All public structs implement Serialize + Deserialize.'

`SmimeError` is a public type (`pub use error::SmimeError`) but does NOT implement `Serialize` or `Deserialize`. This is because it wraps `der::Error` (from the `der` crate), which does not implement those traits.

`CertChainError` (a nested type in `SmimeError::CertChain`) DOES implement `Serialize + Deserialize`, which creates an inconsistent surface.

## What callers cannot do

Callers that want to log, store, or transmit smime-tree error values in serialised form (e.g. JMAP error reporting, tracing spans with structured fields) cannot do so with `SmimeError`. They are forced to call `.to_string()` or format a custom serialisation layer.

## Why this matters for a library

An error type that cannot be serialized forces callers to write bespoke error serialisation. For a library claiming 'all public types implement Serialize + Deserialize', this is an undocumented exception that callers will discover by compile error when they try to `#[derive(Serialize)]` a struct containing `SmimeError`.

## What is needed

Either:
1. Remove the `Serialize + Deserialize` blanket claim from the invariant for error types, or
2. Implement manual serde on `SmimeError` by converting the `der::Error` to a string at serialisation time.

## Files

- `smime-tree/src/error.rs` — `SmimeError` definition
- `smime-tree/CLAUDE.md` — states the invariant
close_reason: Added Serialize/Deserialize via manual impl with SmimeErrorRepr helper. Der variant round-trips through string.
